cards.en:
Think of a school filing cabinet. One box on a form is small. One form is about one student. A folder holds all forms of the same kind. The cabinet holds all the folders. Data is stored the same way, in a hierarchy (levels from small to big).

  • Field: one attribute (property) of an entity, e.g. a student's name. An entity is a thing we store data about.
  • Record: all the fields about one entity, e.g. one student's ID, name, sex, class, class number.
  • File (table): many records with the same record structure, e.g. all students.
  • Database: a collection of related files/tables, e.g. STUDENT + SUBJECT + MARK tables of a school.

Order (small → big): field → record → file → database. Each higher level is a collection of items from the level below.

Exam wording: A record is a collection of fields about one entity. A file is a collection of records with the same structure. A database is a collection of related files.
cards.zh:
想像学校的文件柜：表格上的一格很小；一张表格讲一个学生；一个文件夹放同类表格；整个柜就是全部。数据也是这样分级 (hierarchy) 储存的。

  • Field 字段：实体 (entity，即要记录的对象) 的一个属性，例如姓名。
  • Record 记录：一个实体的所有字段。
  • File (table) 档案/表：结构相同的多条记录。
  • Database 数据库：多个相关的表。

由小到大：field → record → file → database。

考试写法：A record is a collection of fields about one entity.

ex.q: A library stores: (i) the title 'Harry Potter'; (ii) all data about one book; (iii) all books' data; (iv) books + members + loans tables. Name each level.
ex.a:
1. 'Harry Potter' is one attribute → field.
2. All data of one book → record.
3. All books with the same structure → file (table).
4. Several related tables → database.
ex.az: 1. 书名＝field。2. 一本书全部数据＝record。3. 全部书＝file。4. 书、会员、借阅三表＝database。

ex.q: A STUDENT table has 5 fields and 40 students. How many records and how many data items (cells)?
ex.a:
1. One student = one record → 40 records.
2. Each record has 5 fields → 40 × 5 = 200 data items.
ex.az: 1. 每个学生一条记录 → 40 条。2. 40×5＝200 个数据项。

ex.q: A student writes: 'A field is a collection of records.' What is wrong?
ex.a:
1. The order is reversed.
2. Correct: a record is a collection of fields; a field is the smallest level here.
Tip: remember the order field → record → file → database (small → big).
ex.az: 把层级倒转了。正确：record 由 fields 组成，field 是最小一级。

frames.en: Field: 'Tom Ho' is one value of the NAME field.
frames.zh: Field：'Tom Ho' 是 NAME 字段的一个值。

frames.en: Record: SID + NAME + SEX + CLASS + CNO of Tom Ho.
File/table: STUDENT holds every student's record.
Database: STUDENT, SUBJECT and MARK tables, related to each other.

cards.t: Database vs spreadsheet; DBMS and GUI
cards.tz: 数据库 vs 电子表格；DBMS 与 GUI
cards.en:
A spreadsheet is fine for a class mark list. But for a whole school's data (thousands of records, many linked tables, many users), a database is better.

A DBMS (database management system) is software that lets us organise, store and retrieve data efficiently, e.g. Microsoft Access, MySQL.

  • Without GUI: type SQL commands such as SELECT * FROM STUDENT and read text output.
  • With GUI (graphical user interface: windows, buttons): click to sort, filter, add and delete records.
SpreadsheetDatabase
Data sizesmalllarge
Linked tableshardeasy (relationships)
Data rulesloosedata types / validation enforced
Quick charts / what-ifeasyharder

Exam wording: A database is preferred for a large amount of data because a DBMS can organise, store and retrieve data efficiently and reduce data redundancy.
cards.zh:
电子表格适合小量数据，例如一班成绩；全校数据量大、多表相连、多人使用，就用数据库。

DBMS（数据库管理系统）是让我们高效地组织、储存、检索数据的软件，如 Access、MySQL。可不用 GUI（输入 SQL），也可用 GUI（图形界面，点击排序、筛选）。

考试写法：A DBMS can organise, store and retrieve data efficiently.

ex.q: A school keeps 3000 students' records, linked to subjects and marks, used by 50 teachers. Spreadsheet or database? Give 2 reasons.
ex.a:
1. Choose a database.
2. Reason 1: it handles a large amount of data efficiently.
3. Reason 2: tables can be related, so student data is stored once (less data redundancy).
ex.az: 选数据库：数据量大；表可互相关联，减少重复数据。

ex.q: A teacher wants a quick bar chart of 30 marks for one class. Which tool?
ex.a:
1. Small data, needs a chart fast.
2. A spreadsheet is simpler here.
ex.az: 数据少、要快速画图 → 电子表格。

ex.q: 'Using a DBMS GUI means we don't need SQL, so the DBMS is not using SQL.' Correct?
ex.a:
1. Wrong. The GUI is just a friendlier interface.
2. Behind the clicks, the DBMS still runs queries (often SQL).
3. Correct statement: a DBMS can be used with or without a GUI.
ex.az: 错。GUI 只是界面，背后仍执行查询。

demo.setup: CREATE TABLE STUDENT (SID TEXT, ENAME TEXT, SEX TEXT, CLASS TEXT, CNO INTEGER);INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES ('015031','Mary Lee','F','1A',1);INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES ('015032','Tom Ho','M','1A',2);INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES ('015033','Ken Wong','M','1B',1);INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES ('015034','Amy Chan','F','1B',2);INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES ('015035','Ben Lau','M','1A',3);
demo.note: Without a GUI you type SQL like this and read the result table.

cards.en:
If you cook with bad ingredients, the dish is bad, even with a great chef. Computers are the same: wrong input → useless output. This is GIGO, "garbage in, garbage out".

So we use data control to reduce bad input. Two approaches:

  • Data validation: done by the computer, checks data follows rules (reasonable).
  • Data verification: done by humans, checks data matches the source (accurate).

Exam wording: When unreliable or incorrect data is input, the output information will not be useful (GIGO).
cards.zh:
材料坏，厨师再好也煮不出好菜。输入错误数据，输出的资讯就没有用，这叫 GIGO。

所以要做数据控制 (data control)：data validation（电脑自动检查是否合理）和 data verification（人工检查是否与来源一致）。

考试写法：Unreliable input data leads to useless output information (GIGO).

ex.q: A survey typed one student's age as 150. The class average age becomes 22. Explain using GIGO.
ex.a:
1. Input 150 is garbage (unreasonable).
2. The average uses it → output 22 is wrong.
3. GIGO: incorrect input leads to useless output. A range check could stop it.
ex.az: 输入 150 是垃圾数据，平均值因此错。可用 range check 防止。

ex.q: Name the two approaches of data control and who does each.
ex.a:
1. Validation → computer.
2. Verification → humans.
ex.az: validation 电脑；verification 人。

ex.q: 'With a powerful computer, GIGO doesn't happen.' True?
ex.a:
1. False. Speed doesn't fix wrong input.
2. The computer processes whatever it gets; bad input still gives bad output.
3. Only data control reduces GIGO.
ex.az: 错。电脑多快都不能修正错误输入。

cards.en:
Data enters a system by typing, scanning, or network transfer. Mistakes happen at different points:

ErrorMeaningExampleFix
Data source errorthe source itself gives wrong datauser gives a fake emailsend an activation code
Transcription errordata misread, misheard or mistypedOCR reads 'I' as '1'; 冶 typed as 治verification, check digit
Transposition errortwo characters swapped1234 typed as 1324check digit
Transmission errordata changed while sent over a networka bit flips due to noiseparity check

Exam wording: Transposition error: the order of two adjacent characters is swapped.
cards.zh:
输入错误可在不同环节发生：

  • Data source error：来源本身给错（假电邮）。
  • Transcription error：看错、听错、打错。
  • Transposition error：两个字符对调（1234→1324）。
  • Transmission error：网络传送时数据改变 → parity check。

考试写法：Transposition error: two adjacent characters are swapped.

ex.q: Order no. 57281 is typed as 57821. Which error, and what can detect it?
ex.a:
1. '2' and '8' swapped → transposition error.
2. A check digit can detect it.
ex.az: 2 和 8 对调 → transposition；用 check digit。

ex.q: A clerk hears 'fifteen' but types 50. Which error?
ex.a: 1. Misheard → transcription error.
ex.az: 听错 → transcription error。

ex.q: A student says a bit flipped during Wi‑Fi transfer is a 'transcription error'. Correct it.
ex.a:
1. Nobody typed or read it, so not transcription.
2. It changed during transmission → transmission error; detect with a parity check.
ex.az: 不是人打错，是传送时改变 → transmission error，用 parity check。

cards.tz: 数据有效性检验：目的与限制
cards.en:
Validation is like a school gate guard checking uniforms. The guard sees a uniform is correct, but can't tell if you're really in 5A. Validation checks data is reasonable and follows rules, not that it is true.

  • Run automatically by programs, e.g. online booking forms.
  • Many checks can apply to one field (e.g. presence + type + range).
  • Limit: a valid value can still be wrong (age 15 typed instead of 16 passes a range check).

Exam wording: Data validation ensures input data is reasonable and matches certain rules; it cannot guarantee the data is accurate.
cards.zh:
Validation 就像门口检查校服：只看是否合规，不知道你是否真的是该班学生。它检查数据合理、符合规则，不保证正确。

  • 由程序自动执行。
  • 同一字段可用多种检查。
  • 限制：合理的值仍可能是错的。

考试写法：ensures data is reasonable, cannot guarantee accuracy。

ex.q: Age field: list three checks that could apply together.
ex.a:
1. Presence check: not empty.
2. Type check: integer.
3. Range check: 12–20.
ex.az: presence、type、range 可同时用。

ex.q: Mark 67 entered as 76 (range 0–100). Does validation catch it?
ex.a:
1. 76 is in 0–100 → passes.
2. Not caught; need verification (e.g. proofreading).
ex.az: 76 仍在范围内，validation 抓不到，要 verification。

ex.q: 'After validation, data is 100% correct.' Fix this statement.
ex.a:
1. Wrong: validation only checks reasonableness.
2. Correct: validation reduces errors but cannot guarantee accuracy.
ex.az: 错：只保证合理，不保证正确。

cards.t: Presence check and fixed value check
cards.tz: 存在检查与固定值检查
cards.en:
Presence check: a required field must not be empty. Like a form saying "Name *" (required).

Fixed value check: the data must be one of a list of allowed values, e.g. sex ∈ {M, F}, class ∈ {5A, 5B, 5C}.

UI that forces fixed values: drop-down list, radio buttons (choose one), checkboxes (choose several).

Exam wording: Presence check ensures there must be data in a required field. Fixed value check ensures data can only be one of specific values.
cards.zh:
Presence check：必填字段不能留空。Fixed value check：数据只能是指定值之一，如性别 M/F。下拉选单、radio button、checkbox 都自动做到固定值检查。

考试写法：ensures there must be data in a required field。

ex.q: Which check stops a blank email field?
ex.a: 1. Field is empty → presence check.
ex.az: 空白 → presence check。

ex.q: House colour must be Red, Blue, Green or Yellow. Which check and which UI?
ex.a:
1. Limited list → fixed value check.
2. Use a drop-down list or radio buttons.
ex.az: 固定值检查，用下拉选单或 radio button。

ex.q: A student says 'Presence check makes sure the name is correct.' What's wrong?
ex.a:
1. Presence check only checks something was entered.
2. 'xxx' passes it. It says nothing about correctness.
ex.az: presence check 只检查有没有输入，'xxx' 也会通过。

notes.t: Store the input sex (wrong on purpose).
Presence check: is the name empty?

notes.tz: 空白时显示（这里不执行）。

notes.t: Fixed value check: is sex in the allowed list?
notes.tz: Fixed value check：是否在容许列表内？

notes.t: 'X' is not allowed, so this prints.

code.out: Sex must be M or F

cards.en:
Type check: data must be of a certain data type, e.g. age must be a number, not 'sixteen'.

Why it matters: the same field should share one type so we can sort correctly and calculate. Averaging "八十五" and 91 gives an ERROR.

TypeMeaningExample
Integerwhole number74, −29
Real / floating pointhas decimals79.5
Character / stringtext'Tom', '015034'
BooleanTrue/FalsePaid?
Date/timedate25/11/2026

Note: IDs and phone numbers with leading zeros are stored as string, because we never do maths on them and 015034 as a number loses the 0.

Exam wording: Type check ensures the data must be of a certain type.
cards.zh:
Type check：数据必须是某种类型，如年龄必须是数字。同一字段类型一致，才能正确排序和计算。前导 0 的编号用 string。

考试写法：ensures the data must be of a certain type。

ex.q: Choose data types: Weight 52.5; Number of siblings; HKID; Is a prefect?
ex.a:
1. 52.5 → real.
2. siblings → integer.
3. HKID has letters → string.
4. Yes/No → Boolean.
ex.az: real、integer、string、Boolean。

ex.q: Phone numbers sorted as numbers vs as strings: '21234567','91234567','31234567'. Which type and why?
ex.a:
1. We never add phone numbers.
2. Fixed 8 characters; store as string, so leading zeros or '+852' are kept.
ex.az: 电话不用计算，用 string。

ex.q: Student ID 015034 stored as integer. What goes wrong?
ex.a:
1. Integers drop leading zeros → stored as 15034.
2. Wrong ID shown. Correct: use string.
ex.az: 整数会去掉前导 0，变成 15034，应用 string。

cards.en:
Range check: the value must be between limits, e.g. 0 ≤ mark ≤ 100.

Length check: the number of characters must meet a rule, e.g. HK phone = 8 digits; password ≥ 8 characters.

Easy way to remember: range = how big; length = how long.

Exam wording: Range check ensures the data is within a certain range. Length check ensures the length of the data matches certain criteria.
cards.zh:
Range check：数值要在范围内（0–100）。Length check：字符数符合要求（电话 8 位）。range 看「多大」，length 看「多长」。

考试写法：ensures the data is within a certain range。

ex.q: Test mark 105 entered. Which check fails?
ex.a: 1. 105 > 100 → range check fails.
ex.az: 超出 0–100 → range check。

ex.q: Phone '9123456' entered. Which check fails?
ex.a: 1. Count characters: 7, need 8 → length check fails.
ex.az: 只有 7 位 → length check。

ex.q: 'Password must be at least 8 characters' is called a range check. Correct?
ex.a:
1. Wrong: it counts characters, not value.
2. It is a length check.
ex.az: 错，数字符数量是 length check。

cards.tz: 格式、一致性、唯一性检查
cards.en:
• Format check: data follows a pattern, e.g. email contains '@'; date DD/MM/YYYY.
  • Consistency check: data is reasonable compared with other fields, e.g. end date after start date; age matches date of birth.
  • Uniqueness check: no duplicate value in the field, e.g. student ID, one application per student.

Tip: if the rule involves two fields, it's consistency. If it involves all other records, it's uniqueness.

Exam wording: Consistency check ensures data is reasonable when compared to the data in other fields.
cards.zh:
• Format check：符合格式，如电邮有 '@'。
  • Consistency check：与其他字段比较是否合理，如结束日在开始日之后。
  • Uniqueness check：字段内不可重复，如学生编号。

涉及两个字段→consistency；与其他记录比较→uniqueness。

考试写法：reasonable when compared to the data in other fields。

ex.q: Return date 01/03 before borrow date 05/03. Which check?
ex.a: 1. Compares two fields → consistency check.
ex.az: 比较两个字段 → consistency。

ex.q: Two members register with the same username. Which check?
ex.a: 1. Duplicate in the field → uniqueness check.
ex.az: 重复 → uniqueness。

ex.q: Email 'tomho.abc.com' is said to fail a type check. Correct it.
ex.a:
1. It's still text, so type is OK.
2. It lacks '@' → fails a format check.
ex.az: 仍是文字，类型没错；缺 '@' → format check。

cards.en:
Best validation is to stop wrong input before it happens. Instead of a free text box, give limited choices:

UIBuilt-in check
Drop-down listfixed value (one)
Radio buttonsfixed value (one)
Checkboxesfixed value (many)
Date pickertype + format (no 32/08)
Sliderrange

Exam wording: These designs reduce input errors because users can only select valid values.
cards.zh:
最好的方法是一开始就不让人输入错：下拉选单、radio button（单选）、checkbox（多选）、date picker（日期类型与格式）、slider（范围）。

考试写法：reduce input errors，用户只能选有效值。

ex.q: Choose UI: (a) month of birth (b) favourite sports, may pick many (c) satisfaction 1–10.
ex.a:
1. (a) drop-down list.
2. (b) checkboxes.
3. (c) slider (range).
ex.az: 下拉、checkbox、slider。

ex.q: Why is a date picker better than a text box for a booking date?
ex.a:
1. Only real dates can be picked (type check).
2. Format is fixed (format check).
3. Fewer input errors.
ex.az: 只可选真实日期，格式固定。

ex.q: A form uses checkboxes for 'Sex'. What's wrong?
ex.a:
1. Checkboxes allow several choices → could tick both M and F.
2. Use radio buttons or a drop-down (one value).
ex.az: checkbox 可多选，应用 radio button。

cards.en:
A check digit is an extra digit added to the end of a number, calculated from the other digits by an algorithm (fixed rule). Used for HKID, ISBN, credit cards.

How it works: when the number is entered, the computer re-calculates. If the result doesn't match, the number is invalid. It catches transcription and transposition errors.

Exam wording: A check digit is generated by a specific algorithm and appended to the end of the numeric data. If it does not match, the data is invalid.
cards.zh:
Check digit 是由算法根据其他数字算出，加在数字尾的位。输入时电脑重算，不符就无效，可侦测打错和对调。

考试写法：generated by a specific algorithm and appended to the end of the numeric data。

ex.q: Simple rule: check digit = sum of digits mod 10. Find it for 4725.
Using the same rule, is 47268 valid?
ex.az: 算出 9≠8，无效。

ex.q: With the sum rule, 4725 typed as 7425 still gives 8. A student says check digits catch every swap. Correct?
ex.a:
1. Sum is unchanged by swapping → not detected.
2. That's why real schemes (HKID) use weights: position matters.
ex.az: 简单相加抓不到对调，所以要用加权 (weights)。

cards.tz: 香港身份证查数位算法
cards.en:
HKID = 1–2 letters + 6 digits + check digit in brackets (0–9 or A). The weights make position matter, so swaps are caught.

  1. Remove brackets. If only one letter, put a space in front (now 9 characters with check digit).
  2. Values: space = 36, A = 10, B = 11 … Z = 35; digits = themselves.
  3. Multiply by weights 9, 8, 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1, then add → weighted sum.
  4. Valid if weighted sum mod 11 = 0.

To find the check digit: r = (weighted sum of first 8) mod 11; check digit = 11 − r. 10 → A, 11 (r=0) → 0.

Exam wording: The HKID is valid if the weighted sum is divisible by 11.
cards.zh:
步骤：去括号；只有一个字母就前面加空格；空格=36、A=10…Z=35；乘权重 9,8,…,1 相加；总和能被 11 整除就有效。求查数位：r=前 8 位加权和 mod 11，查数位=11−r（10→A，11→0）。

考试写法：valid if the weighted sum is divisible by 11。

ex.q: Find the check digit of A123456.
ex.a:
1. One letter → '␣A123456'.
2.
charvalueweightproduct
␣369324
A10880
1177
22612
33515
44416
55315
66212
3. Sum = 481.
4. 481 mod 11 = 8 (11×43=473).
5. 11 − 8 = 3 → A123456(3).

ex.q: Is Y147036(A) valid?
A student finds r = 0 and writes check digit 11. What's wrong?
ex.a:
1. Check digit must be a single character.
2. 11 − 0 = 11 → rule says use 0.
3. Also 10 → 'A', not '10'.
ex.az: r=0 时查数位是 0，不是 11；10 写作 A。

ex.q: Forgetting the space: a student uses weights 8..1 on 'A123456(3)' without the space value. Result?
ex.a:
1. Missing ␣×9 = 324 changes the sum.
2. 484 − 324 = 160, 160 mod 11 = 6 ≠ 0 → wrongly 'invalid'.
3. Always add the space (36) for single-letter IDs.
ex.az: 漏了空格(36×9)，结果错判无效。

frames.en: One letter → add a space: ␣ A 1 2 3 4 5 6 3
frames.zh: 只有一个字母 → 前加空格。

frames.en: ␣=36, A=10, digits stay.
484 = 11 × 44, remainder 0 → valid.

notes.t: Define a function taking the ID without check digit.
notes.tz: 定义函数，输入不含查数位的号码。
7 个字符表示只有一个字母。

notes.t: Pair each character with weights 9 down to 2.
notes.tz: 每个字符配权重 9 至 2。

cards.en:
When bits travel over a network, noise can flip a 0 to 1. A parity bit is one extra bit added so the total number of 1s is even (even parity) or odd (odd parity). The receiver counts the 1s; if the count is wrong, there's an error.

Data1sEven parityOdd parity
101100141011001010110011
111001151110011111100110

Limits: if two (an even number of) bits flip, the count is still right → not detected. It also cannot tell which bit is wrong, so can't correct it.

Exam wording: A parity bit is added so that the total number of 1s is even (even parity) / odd (odd parity). It cannot detect an even number of bit errors.
cards.zh:
传送时噪音可能令位元翻转。加一个同位位元 (parity bit)，令1 的总数为偶数 (even parity) 或奇数 (odd parity)。接收方数 1，不符即出错。限制：两个位元同时出错侦测不到，也不知道哪一位错。

考试写法：total number of 1s is even/odd；cannot detect an even number of bit errors。

ex.q: Add an even parity bit to 1011001.
ex.a:
1. Count 1s: 1,0,1,1,0,0,1 → 4.
2. 4 is even → parity bit 0.
3. Result 10110010.
ex.az: 4 个 1 已是偶数，加 0。

ex.q: Even parity. Received 11010110. Error?
ex.a:
1. Count 1s: 1+1+0+1+0+1+1+0 = 5.
2. 5 is odd but should be even → error detected.
ex.az: 5 个 1，是奇数 → 出错。

ex.q: Even parity: sent 10110010, received 01110010. Student says 'no error'. Explain.
ex.a:
1. Count 1s in received: 0+1+1+1+0+0+1+0 = 4 → even, check passes.
2. But the first two bits both flipped → two-bit error not detected.
3. So 'passes parity check' ≠ 'no error'.
ex.az: 两位同时翻转，1 的数目仍是偶数，侦测不到。

frames.en: 1011001 has four 1s.
Even already → append 0 → 10110010.
One bit flips: received 10100010.
Receiver counts 3 ones → odd → error detected, ask to resend.
frames.zh: 3 个 1 → 奇数 → 侦测到错误，要求重传。

code.src:
def even_parity(bits):
    ones = bits.count('1')
    p = '0' if ones % 2 == 0 else '1'
    return bits + p
print(even_parity('1011001'))
print(even_parity('1110011'))

cards.en:
Verification = humans check the data was copied correctly from the source.

  • Inputting data twice: the same person types it twice; the computer compares. E.g. 'confirm password'.
  • Double data entry: two different operators type the same data independently; copies compared. E.g. survey forms.
  • Proofreading: another person compares the entered data with the original document.

Exam wording: Verification checks whether the data is accurate and consistent when transferred from the source.
cards.zh:
Verification：人工检查数据是否与来源一致。

  • Inputting twice：同一人输入两次（确认密码）。
  • Double data entry：两个人各自输入，再比较。
  • Proofreading：另一人对照原文件检查。

考试写法：whether the data is accurate and consistent with the source。

ex.q: Why do sign-up forms ask you to type the new password twice?
ex.a:
1. You can't see the password (hidden).
2. Typing twice and comparing catches typos → inputting data twice.
ex.az: 密码看不到，打两次比较 → inputting twice。

ex.q: 500 paper questionnaires must be entered accurately. Suggest a method.
ex.a:
1. Double data entry: two operators each enter all forms.
2. Computer compares; differences are checked against paper.
ex.az: 两人各自输入再比较。

ex.q: A student says double data entry means one person typing twice. Correct it.
ex.a:
1. That's inputting data twice.
2. Double data entry needs two different operators working independently, so the same habit-error isn't repeated.
ex.az: 一人两次是 inputting twice；double entry 要两个人。

cards.en:
ValidationVerification
Whocomputer, automatichuman
Checksdata is reasonable, follows rulesdata is accurate, same as source
Examplespresence, fixed value, type, range, length, format, consistency, uniqueness, check digit, parityinput twice, double data entry, proofreading

Use both: validation stops impossible data; verification catches possible-but-wrong data.

Exam wording: Validation ensures data is reasonable; verification ensures data is accurate. Neither alone guarantees correct data.
cards.zh:
Validation：电脑自动，检查合理。Verification：人工，检查准确（与来源一致）。两者一起用。

考试写法：validation → reasonable；verification → accurate。

ex.q: Mark 'abc' typed into a mark field. Which control catches it?
ex.a: 1. Not a number → validation (type check).
ex.az: validation（type check）。

ex.q: Mark 67 typed as 76. Which control catches it?
ex.a:
1. 76 is reasonable → validation passes.
2. Comparing with paper → verification (proofreading).
ex.az: verification（校对）。

ex.q: 'Check digit is a verification method because it checks accuracy.' Correct?
ex.a: 1. Wrong. It's calculated by the computer automatically → validation.
ex.az: 错，电脑自动计算 → validation。

cards.en:
A database stores data in a planned structure: which tables, which fields, which data types. Good structure:

  • lets tables link (communicate) with each other;
  • reduces data redundancy (the same data stored many times);
  • right data types → data consistency and easy analysis.
FieldTypeWhy
SIDStringkeep leading 0 (015034)
ENAMEStringtext
CNOIntegersort 1,2,…,10 correctly

Exam wording: A good database structure reduces data redundancy and enables communication between tables.
cards.zh:
数据库按结构组织数据。好结构令表可互相关联、减少数据冗余（重复储存），选对类型有助一致性与分析。

考试写法：reduces data redundancy。

ex.q: Class teacher's name is typed in every student record. Problem and fix?
ex.a:
1. Same data repeated → data redundancy; if the teacher changes, many records to update.
2. Fix: a separate CLASS table storing teacher once, linked by CLASS.
ex.az: 重复储存 → 冗余；另设 CLASS 表。

ex.q: Why store CNO as integer rather than string?
ex.a:
1. As strings, '10' sorts before '2'.
2. As integers, 1,2,…,10 sorts correctly.
ex.az: 字符串排序 '10' 会排在 '2' 前。

ex.q: A student stores DOB as string '5/3/2010'. Problem?
ex.a:
1. Can't easily calculate age or sort by date ('12/1' vs '5/3' sorts wrong).
2. Use date type.
ex.az: 日期用 string 不能正确排序或计算，应用 date 类型。

demo.setup: CREATE TABLE T (CNO_TEXT TEXT, CNO_INT INTEGER);INSERT INTO T VALUES ('2',2);INSERT INTO T VALUES ('10',10);INSERT INTO T VALUES ('1',1);
demo.query: SELECT CNO_TEXT FROM T ORDER BY CNO_TEXT
demo.note: As text, '10' comes before '2'. Try ORDER BY CNO_INT instead.

cards.en:
We can insert, update and delete records with SQL (Structured Query Language) or a GUI. For many records, import a .csv file (comma-separated values) instead of typing.

Exam wording: Records can be inserted, changed or deleted using SQL or a GUI; data can be imported from .csv files to save time.
cards.zh:
可用 SQL 或 GUI 新增、修改、删除记录；大量数据可汇入 .csv 档，省时。

考试写法：imported from .csv files to save time。

ex.q: Insert student 015036, 'Joe Ma', M, 1B, 3.
ex.a:
1. 
INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES ('015036','Joe Ma','M','1B',3);
2. SID in quotes (string).
ex.az: SID 用引号，因为是字符串。

ex.q: Tom Ho moves to 1B. Write SQL.
ex.a:
1. 
UPDATE STUDENT SET CLASS = '1B' WHERE SID = '015032';
ex.az: 用 UPDATE … WHERE。

ex.q: A student writes DELETE FROM STUDENT; to remove Ben Lau. Result?
ex.a:
1. No WHERE → all records deleted.
2. Correct: DELETE FROM STUDENT WHERE SID = '015035';
ex.az: 没有 WHERE 会删除全部记录。

demo.setup: CREATE TABLE STUDENT (SID TEXT, ENAME TEXT, SEX TEXT, CLASS TEXT, CNO INTEGER);INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES ('015031','Mary Lee','F','1A',1);INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES ('015032','Tom Ho','M','1A',2);INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES ('015033','Ken Wong','M','1B',1);INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES ('015034','Amy Chan','F','1B',2);INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES ('015035','Ben Lau','M','1A',3);INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES ('015036','Joe Ma','M','1B',3);
demo.note: Joe Ma was added by INSERT.

code.src:
INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES ('015036','Joe Ma','M','1B',3);
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM STUDENT;

notes.t: Add one new record to STUDENT.

code.setup: CREATE TABLE STUDENT (SID TEXT, ENAME TEXT, SEX TEXT, CLASS TEXT, CNO INTEGER);INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES ('015031','Mary Lee','F','1A',1);INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES ('015032','Tom Ho','M','1A',2);INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES ('015033','Ken Wong','M','1B',1);INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES ('015034','Amy Chan','F','1B',2);INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES ('015035','Ben Lau','M','1A',3);

cards.tz: 数据库功能：检索与排序
cards.en:
Retrieval = getting only the data you need. Sorting = putting it in order.

  • WHERE picks rows that meet a condition.
  • ORDER BY field sorts ascending (A→Z, small→big); add DESC for descending.

Exam wording: Data can be retrieved by specific criteria and sorted in ascending or descending order.
cards.zh:
检索：只取需要的数据（WHERE）。排序：ORDER BY，默认升序，DESC 降序。

考试写法：retrieved by criteria and sorted。

ex.q: List male students.
ex.a:
1. 
SELECT * FROM STUDENT WHERE SEX = 'M';
2. Result: Tom Ho, Ken Wong, Ben Lau.
ex.az: WHERE SEX='M'。

ex.q: List male students by name A→Z.
ex.a:
1. 
SELECT * FROM STUDENT WHERE SEX = 'M' ORDER BY ENAME;
2. Order: Ben Lau, Ken Wong, Tom Ho.
ex.az: 加 ORDER BY ENAME。

ex.q: A student writes SELECT * FROM STUDENT ORDER BY ENAME WHERE SEX='M';
ex.a:
1. Syntax error: WHERE must come before ORDER BY.
2. Correct: … WHERE SEX='M' ORDER BY ENAME;
ex.az: WHERE 必须在 ORDER BY 前。

demo.setup: CREATE TABLE STUDENT (SID TEXT, ENAME TEXT, SEX TEXT, CLASS TEXT, CNO INTEGER);INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES ('015031','Mary Lee','F','1A',1);INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES ('015032','Tom Ho','M','1A',2);INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES ('015033','Ken Wong','M','1B',1);INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES ('015034','Amy Chan','F','1B',2);INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES ('015035','Ben Lau','M','1A',3);
demo.query: SELECT * FROM STUDENT WHERE SEX = 'M' ORDER BY ENAME
demo.note: Rows with SEX = 'M' are kept, then sorted by name.

notes.t: Show only the name column from STUDENT.

code.out:
Ben Lau
Ken Wong
Tom Ho
code.setup: CREATE TABLE STUDENT (SID TEXT, ENAME TEXT, SEX TEXT, CLASS TEXT, CNO INTEGER);INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES ('015031','Mary Lee','F','1A',1);INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES ('015032','Tom Ho','M','1A',2);INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES ('015033','Ken Wong','M','1B',1);INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES ('015034','Amy Chan','F','1B',2);INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES ('015035','Ben Lau','M','1A',3);

cards.t: Index: how it speeds up retrieval
cards.en:
Like the index at the back of a textbook: you don't read every page; you look up the word in a sorted list and jump to the page.

  • Without an index: the DBMS checks records one by one (worst case: every record).
  • With an index: an index table stores the indexed field (sorted) + a pointer (location) to the record. Each check removes about half of what's left (binary search).

For 11 records: up to 11 checks without index, at most 4 with index (24 = 16 ≥ 11).

Exam wording: An index table contains the indexed field and a pointer to the related record; since it is sorted, records can be found faster.
cards.zh:
像课本后面的索引：在已排序的列表找字，再跳去该页。没有索引要逐条查；有索引，索引表存已排序的字段 + 指向记录的指针，每次排除约一半（二分搜寻）。11 条记录最多 4 次。

考试写法：the indexed field and a pointer to the related record。

ex.q: Find 'Peter Chan' in a sorted index of 11 names. How many checks?
ex.a:
1. Middle-first search, each check halves the list.
2. It takes 4 checks here (see the demo).
3. Maximum for 11 items: 4.
ex.az: 二分搜寻，这里用 4 次。

ex.q: Max checks with an index for 1000 records?
ex.a:
1. Find smallest n with 2n ≥ 1000.
2. 210 = 1024 → 10 checks (vs up to 1000 without).

ex.q: 'The index table stores a full copy of every record.' Correct?
ex.a:
1. Wrong. It stores only the indexed field + pointer.
2. The full record stays in the main table.
ex.az: 错，只存被索引的字段和指针。

frames.en: Middle = #6 'Liliana Ko'. P comes after → discard #1–#6.
frames.zh: 中间 #6 'Liliana Ko'，P 在后 → 丢掉前半。

frames.en: Middle = #9 'Queenie Fu'. P comes before → discard #9–#11.
frames.zh: 中间 #9 'Queenie Fu'，P 在前 → 丢掉后半。

frames.en: Middle = #7 'Nolan Tse'. P comes after → discard #7–#7.
frames.zh: 中间 #7 'Nolan Tse'，P 在后 → 丢掉前半。

frames.en: Middle = #8 'Peter Chan' → found; follow the pointer to the record.
frames.zh: 中间 #8 'Peter Chan' → 找到，跟指针取记录。

cards.en:
An index is not free, like keeping a contact list in order: every new friend means re-arranging.

  • The index must be updated when the indexed value changes or a record is added/deleted → takes time (slower insert/update).
  • The index table needs extra storage space.

So index only fields that are searched often; don't index every field.

Exam wording: Indexing speeds up searching but needs extra storage and time to update the index when data changes.
cards.zh:
索引有代价：资料改变或新增时要更新索引（花时间），索引表也要额外储存空间。只为经常搜寻的字段建索引。

考试写法：extra storage 和 time to update the index。

ex.q: Should a school index SID on STUDENT?
ex.a:
1. SID is searched very often.
2. Benefit > cost → yes.
ex.az: SID 常被搜寻 → 应建索引。

ex.q: A log table gets 10,000 new rows per minute and is rarely searched. Index it?
ex.a:
1. Every insert updates the index → slow.
2. Rarely searched → little benefit → no.
ex.az: 插入极频繁、少搜寻 → 不建。

ex.q: 'Indexing makes the database file smaller.' Correct?
ex.a:
1. Wrong: the index table is extra data.
2. It increases storage.
ex.az: 错，索引会增加储存空间。

demo.setup: CREATE TABLE STUDENT (SID TEXT, ENAME TEXT, SEX TEXT, CLASS TEXT, CNO INTEGER);INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES ('015031','Mary Lee','F','1A',1);INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES ('015032','Tom Ho','M','1A',2);INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES ('015033','Ken Wong','M','1B',1);INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES ('015034','Amy Chan','F','1B',2);INSERT INTO STUDENT VALUES ('015035','Ben Lau','M','1A',3);CREATE INDEX idx_name ON STUDENT(ENAME);
demo.query: SELECT * FROM STUDENT WHERE ENAME = 'Tom Ho'
demo.note: CREATE INDEX builds a sorted index on ENAME; searches by name use it.

cards.en:
Like a cassette tape or a video with no skip button: to hear song 5, you must play past songs 1–4.

Sequential access: data is written in order from the beginning, and to reach a record the device must go through all records before it.

  • Device: magnetic tape.
  • Speed depends on where the data is; on average slower than direct access.
  • Good for processing a whole file in order, e.g. backup, monthly payroll.

Exam wording: In sequential access, data must be accessed in order from the beginning; access time depends on the location of the data.
cards.zh:
像录音带：要听第 5 首，要先经过 1–4 首。Sequential access：数据由头顺序写入，读取时要经过前面所有数据。装置：磁带。速度视位置而定，平均较慢；适合备份等整份顺序处理。

考试写法：accessed in order from the beginning。

ex.q: Tape holds records 1–100. How many records are passed to read record 60 (from start)?
ex.a:
1. Must pass records 1–59.
2. 59 passed, read the 60th.
ex.az: 要经过 59 条。

ex.q: Why is tape fine for nightly backup?
ex.a:
1. Backup writes/reads the whole data in order anyway.
2. Tape is cheap per GB.
ex.az: 备份本来就顺序处理，磁带便宜。

ex.q: 'Sequential access always takes the same time.' Correct?
ex.a:
1. Wrong: record 1 is fast, record 100 is slow.
2. Time varies with location.
ex.az: 错，时间视位置而定。

frames.en: Head at record 1.
Must pass R1, R2, R3, R4…
5 steps to read R5.
Hard disk: go straight to the address of R5 in one jump.
frames.zh: 硬盘：直接跳到 R5 的地址。

cards.en:
Like a phone's music app: tap song 5 and it plays at once. Direct (random) access: every storage position has a unique address, so data can be read directly without passing other data.

  • Devices: hard disk, SSD, USB flash drive, optical disc (CD/DVD), floppy disk, memory card.
  • Speed stable and generally faster.
  • Good for looking up one record quickly, e.g. a price at a supermarket checkout (POS).

Exam wording: In direct access, each storage location has a unique address so data can be accessed directly without searching through other locations.
cards.zh:
像手机音乐 app，点第 5 首即播。Direct access：每个位置有唯一地址，可直接读取。装置：硬盘、SSD、USB、光碟、软碟。速度稳定且较快，适合快速查一条记录（如收银机查价）。

考试写法：each storage location has a unique address。

ex.q: A supermarket POS looks up a product's price by barcode. Which access?
ex.a: 1. Needs one record fast → direct access (hard disk/SSD).
ex.az: 要快速取一条记录 → direct。

ex.q: Give two devices with direct access.
ex.a:
1. Hard disk.
2. USB flash drive (also SSD, optical disc).
ex.az: 硬盘、USB。

ex.q: 'Direct access means data must be stored in sorted order.' Correct?
ex.a:
1. Wrong: data can be written in any position.
2. The address finds it, not the order.
ex.az: 错，靠地址找，不需排序。

cards.en:
Magnetic tapeHard disk
Access methodSequentialDirect
Access speedunpredictable, lowerstable, higher
Cost per GBlowerhigher
Portabilityhigherlower
Lifespanlongershorter
Usagebackup / archivefrequently used data

Exam wording: Magnetic tape is used for backup because it has a lower cost per unit capacity and longer lifespan, and backup is done sequentially.
cards.zh:
磁带：顺序存取、每 GB 较便宜、寿命较长 → 备份。硬盘：直接存取、速度稳定较快 → 常用数据。

考试写法：tape 用于 backup：lower cost per unit capacity、longer lifespan。

ex.q: A bank keeps 10 years of old records, rarely read. Tape or disk?
ex.a:
1. Huge, rarely accessed, must last long.
2. Tape: cheap per GB, long lifespan.
ex.az: 磁带：便宜、寿命长。

ex.q: An online shop's product database. Tape or disk?
ex.a:
1. Many random lookups every second.
2. Hard disk/SSD (direct access).
ex.az: 硬盘：要随机快速存取。

ex.q: 'DVDs are sequential like tape.' Correct?
ex.a: 1. Wrong. Optical discs support direct access (you can jump to any chapter).
ex.az: 错，光碟是直接存取。

mc.q: Which of the following shows the data hierarchy from the lowest level to the highest level?
mc.e: Field, record, file (table), database.
mc.ez: 由低到高：字段、记录、档案、数据库。
mc.src: Textbook A1 Ch2 Checkpoint 2.3 Q1 (p.51)

mc.q:
Which of the following statements about indexing is/are correct?
(1) Indexing increases the efficiency of data retrieval.
(2) Indexing reduces the storage size of a database.
(3) Index tables need to be updated when new records are added.
mc.e: Index tables take extra space, so (2) is wrong.
mc.ez: 索引需额外空间，(2) 错。
mc.src: Textbook A1 Ch2 Checkpoint 2.3 Q2 (p.51)

mc.q: A school's 8-digit student ID contains a check digit so that the sum of all 8 digits is divisible by 12. Which ID is valid?
mc.e: Digit sums: 22, 24, 20, 30. Only 24 is divisible by 12.
mc.ez: 只有 24 可被 12 整除。
mc.src: Textbook A1 Ch2 Checkpoint 2.1 Q1 (p.40)

mc.q: Using the same rule (sum of 8 digits divisible by 12), Ryan's ID is x646 0878. What is x?
mc.src: Textbook A1 Ch2 Checkpoint 2.1 Q2 (p.40, adapted options)

mc.q:
A feedback website replaces 1–5 sliders with text boxes. Which validations should be applied?
(1) Uniqueness check (2) Type check (3) Range check
mc.e: Ratings must be numbers within 1–5; different customers can give the same rating.
mc.ez: 评分要是数字且在范围内，可重复。
mc.src: Textbook A1 Ch2 Checkpoint 2.1 Q3 (p.41)

mc.q:
An operator mistyped 8-bit code 0010 0000 as 0100 000. Which can find this error?
(1) Double data entry (2) Parity check (3) Length check
mc.e: Both codes have one '1', so parity cannot detect; length 7 ≠ 8 and double entry would differ.
mc.ez: 1 的个数相同，奇偶检验无效。
mc.src: Textbook A1 Ch2 Checkpoint 2.2 Q1 (p.44)

mc.q: Which of the following statements about data validation is correct?
o: Data validation can detect and prevent all errors in data.
Parity checking is an example of data validation.
Proofreading is an appropriate validation method for gender.
Data validation always requires manual effort to complete.
mc.e: Parity check is done automatically by computers, so it is validation.
mc.src: Textbook A1 Ch2 Chapter Exercise MC1 (p.54)

mc.q:
An app requires users to call the company using the input phone number to complete registration. Which error(s) can this prevent?
(1) Data source error (2) Runtime error (3) Transposition error
mc.e: A wrong/fake number (source) or swapped digits would make the call fail, so both are caught.
mc.ez: 号码错误或数字对调都会令来电失败。
mc.src: Textbook A1 Ch2 Chapter Exercise MC2 (p.54)

mc.q: In a database storing personal information of students in a school, which might be the content of a record?
o: The personal information of every student in the school
The personal information of students in class 1A
The personal information of a particular student in 1A
The HKID number of a particular student in 1A
mc.e: A record = all fields about one entity. D is a field.
mc.ez: 记录是一个学生的全部资料。
mc.src: Textbook A1 Ch2 Chapter Exercise MC3 (p.54)

mc.q: Which statement about data hierarchy is incorrect?
o: It is possible for a field to have many records.
It is possible for a file to have many records.
It is possible for a database to have many files.
It is possible for a database to have many fields.
mc.e: A record contains fields, not the reverse.
mc.src: Textbook A1 Ch2 Chapter Exercise MC4 (p.54)

mc.q:
To check for transcription errors in an HKID, which can be used?
(1) Length check (2) Parity check (3) Check digit
mc.e: Parity check is for binary transmission, not HKID entry.
mc.ez: 奇偶检验用于二进制传输。
mc.src: Textbook A1 Ch2 Chapter Exercise MC5 (p.54)

mc.q: A fixed-length product serial number looks like 0000123456789000. The most suitable validation rule is
mc.e: Stored as a number, leading zeros would be lost, so it must be text of length 16.
mc.src: Textbook A1 Ch2 Chapter Exercise MC6 (p.54)

mc.q: Which is an example of data verification when changing a social media password?
o: Click a link sent to the user's email.
Require the user to login again.
Require a password longer than 8 characters.
mc.e: Inputting data twice is verification; D is a length check (validation).
mc.src: Textbook A1 Ch2 Chapter Exercise MC7 (p.54)

mc.q: A database is frequently searched. Which measure cannot speed up searching?
o: Split the records into different files.
Perform indexing on the database records.
Copy the database's content into a spreadsheet file.
Store the database in a direct access medium instead of a sequential one.
mc.e: A spreadsheet is not more efficient for searching large data.
mc.src: Textbook A1 Ch2 Chapter Exercise MC8 (p.54)

mc.q: A database backup is made on magnetic tapes. Which is correct?
o: An optical disc also supports only sequential access.
Retrieving one particular file will likely take longer than from a direct access medium.
The tape can replace hard disks in a computer.
Searching can be done quickly from the tape.
mc.e: Tape is sequential, so finding one file requires passing earlier data.
mc.src: Textbook A1 Ch2 Chapter Exercise MC9 (p.55)

mc.q:
Advantage(s) of a drop-down list over a text box:
(1) Fixed value check is automatically applied. (2) Check digit is automatically calculated. (3) It reduces input error.
mc.e: Drop-down lists do not compute check digits.
mc.ez: 下拉清单不计算查数位。
mc.src: Textbook A1 Ch2 Chapter Exercise MC10 (p.55)

mc.q:
To validate an HKID number by check digit, we should:
(1) Ensure it starts with one or two letters. (2) Ensure its weighted sum is divisible by 11. (3) Ensure its length is no longer than 9.
mc.e: (1) is format check and (3) length check; only (2) is the check digit method.
mc.src: Textbook A1 Ch2 Example 2.1 Q1 (p.39)

mc.q: Four codes received, only one passes the parity check: which?
mc.e: 1s: 4, 6, 3, 2. Only one passes, so odd parity; C has 3.
mc.ez: 只有 C 有奇数个 1。
mc.src: Textbook A1 Ch2 Example 2.1 Q2 (p.40)

mc.q:
An email-change form shows: 'This field is required', 'Invalid email address' (missing @), 'Please enter the same email address'. Methods seen:
(1) Type check (2) Presence check (3) Verification by inputting data twice
mc.e: Missing '@' is a format check, not a type check.
mc.src: Textbook A1 Ch2 Example 2.2 (p.43)

mc.q:
For the field CNO (class number, Number) in a table for Class 1A students only, which checks are suitable?
(1) Uniqueness (2) Type (3) Presence
mc.e: Same class → unique; numeric → type; every student has one → presence.
mc.src: Textbook A1 Ch2 Example 2.3 (p.50)

mc.q: Which level of the data hierarchy is a collection of records sharing the same record structure?
mc.e: A file/table holds records of the same structure.

mc.q: In a STUDENT table displayed in a DBMS, a single column such as ENAME corresponds to a
mc.e: Columns are fields; rows are records.

mc.q: A school database contains STUDENT, TEACHER and CLASSROOM tables. The database is best described as
o: a collection of fields about one entity
a collection of records of one structure
mc.e: Database = collection of related files.

mc.q: Which is NOT a function of a DBMS described in this chapter?
mc.e: DBMS organises, stores and retrieves data.

mc.q: 'Garbage in, garbage out' means
o: the recycle bin must be emptied
unreliable input data produces useless output information
mc.e: GIGO describes the effect of bad input.

mc.q: A cashier records $15 as $51. This is a
mc.e: Two adjacent digits reversed.

mc.q: An OCR program reads capital letter 'I' as the digit '1'. This is a
mc.e: Misread data is a transcription error.

mc.q: A user registers with an email address that does not exist. Which is the best solution suggested?
o: Send an activation code to the email and ask the user to enter it
mc.e: Activation code confirms the source is real.

mc.q: Which is done by computers rather than humans?
o: Comparing a printout with exam papers
mc.e: Validation such as range check is automatic.

mc.q: Which statement about data validation is correct?
o: It guarantees input data is accurate.
It can only be applied once to each field.
It must be done by two operators.
It ensures input data is reasonable and matches certain rules.
mc.e: Validation checks reasonableness; several checks can apply to one field.

mc.q: An application form rejects an age of 10 because applicants must be older than 12. Which check?
mc.e: Value outside a range.

mc.q: A form rejects an applicant whose student ID has already applied. Which check?
mc.e: Duplicate values are not allowed.

mc.q: A form rejects '32/08/2025' as a date. This is mainly a
mc.e: Not a valid date value → type check (date picker prevents it).

mc.q: A form requires the return date to be later than the departure date. This is a
mc.e: Compared with another field.

mc.q: Which UI element allows multiple values to be selected while still applying a fixed value check?
mc.e: Checkboxes allow multiple selections.

mc.q: A date picker mainly provides which checks?
mc.e: Only valid dates in a fixed format.

mc.q: Which data type is most suitable for 'whether a student passes the test'?
mc.e: TRUE/FALSE.

mc.q: Which data type is most suitable for a student's height in metres?
mc.e: Needs decimal places.

mc.q: Why is the average of "八十五", "Seventy two", 91 and 79.5 an error?
o: The field mixes text and numbers, so arithmetic cannot be done
mc.e: Same field should share the same data type.

mc.q: Using the HKID algorithm (space=36, A=10…Z=35, weights 9 to 1, valid if weighted sum divisible by 11), what is the check digit of A123456?
Using the HKID algorithm, which number is valid?
mc.e: WX135135(2) weighted sum 627 = 11×57.

mc.q: The weighted sum of the first 8 characters of an HKID is 690. What is the check digit?
For an HKID with only one letter, what is placed at the beginning before calculation?
mc.e: Whitespace = 36.

mc.q: Under even parity, what is the parity bit for 1110 011?
mc.e: Five 1s → add 1 to make six.

mc.q: Under odd parity, which code (8 bits including parity bit) is correct?
mc.e: 1110 0110 has five 1s.

mc.q: A code 1011 0010 is sent with even parity and two bits are flipped during transmission. The parity check will
mc.e: Flipping two bits keeps the number of 1s even.

mc.q: Two clerks type the same paper questionnaires independently and the computer compares the copies. This is
mc.e: Two operators, independent entries.

mc.q: After entering marks, a teacher prints the mark sheet and checks it against the exam papers. This is
mc.e: Comparing with the original document.

mc.q: Why should a student ID like 015034 be stored as a string?
o: A number cannot have leading zeros
mc.e: 015034 as a number becomes 15034.

mc.q: Which SQL statement retrieves records of male students only?
o: SELECT * FROM STUDENT ORDER BY SEX;
mc.e: WHERE filters rows.

mc.q: Table STUDENT(ENAME, SEX) holds ('Zack','M'),('Aaisha','F'),('Caspian','M'),('Nolan','M'). What is the first row of SELECT ENAME FROM STUDENT WHERE SEX='M' ORDER BY ENAME?
mc.e: Male names sorted: Caspian, Nolan, Zack.
mc.ez: 男生按字母排序第一个是 Caspian。

mc.q: Which is a quick way to create a large number of records in a database?
mc.e: Import comma-separated values.

mc.q: An index table contains
o: the parity bit of each record
the indexed field and a pointer to the related record
copies of all fields of every record
mc.e: Indexed field + pointer.

mc.q: A sorted index has 11 names. In the worst case, how many checks are needed using the halving method?
mc.e: Each check discards about half: 11→5→2→1.

mc.q: Which situation requires the index on ENAME to be updated?
o: A new student record is added
mc.e: New records (or changed names) must be put into the index.

mc.q: Why is indexing too many fields not recommended?
o: Updating indexes takes time and they take storage space
Indexes only work on magnetic tape
mc.e: Costs of time and space.

mc.q: Which device uses sequential access only?
mc.e: Magnetic tape.

mc.q: Compared with a hard disk, a magnetic tape has
mc.e: Tape: cheaper, more portable, longer lifespan.

mc.q: Why is direct access faster on average than sequential access?
o: Direct access devices are always newer
Each storage position has a unique address so data can be reached without passing other data
mc.e: Unique addresses allow jumping directly.

mc.q: Accessing the 5th element after processing all elements before it describes
mc.e: Definition of sequential access.

sq.q: Mr Chan made a website with a registration form containing the fields Username, Email, Password and Confirm Password.

parts.q: For the Username field, suggest TWO validation checks that could be used.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer:
Presence check: username must be entered (1)
Uniqueness check: username must not already exist / Length check: e.g. 6–20 characters (1)

parts.q: Mr Chan used a format check by validating that the Email field contains an '@'. Suggest an invalid email address that would pass the check and a better validation rule.
parts.ms:
e.g. 'tom@' or '@@abc' (1)
Better rule: exactly one '@', with characters before it and a domain containing a '.' after it (1)

parts.q: Explain why only the Password field requires data verification.
parts.ms: The password is hidden (masked) when typed, so the user cannot see typing mistakes; entering it twice confirms it is what the user intended (1)

sq.src: Textbook A1 Ch2 Chapter Exercise LQ1 (p.55)

sq.q: Mr Wong, an inventory manager, inputs product quantities from a handwritten table into an electronic spreadsheet.

parts.q: State two common data errors that would occur during this process.
parts.ms:
Transcription error, e.g. misreading handwriting / mistyping (1)
Transposition error, e.g. 15 typed as 51 (1)

parts.q: State two data verification methods that would help prevent these errors. Explain briefly.
parts.ms:
Double data entry: two people enter the data independently (1); the copies are compared and differences show errors (1)
Proofreading: another person compares the entered data with the handwritten table (1); mistyped/misplaced values can be spotted (1)

sq.src: Textbook A1 Ch2 Chapter Exercise LQ2 (p.55)

sq.q: At a supermarket, the products' information is stored in a database.

parts.q: Which mode of access should be used when searching the database for a product's price? Explain briefly.
parts.ms: Direct access (1); the product record can be located directly by its address without reading other records, so lookup is fast (1)

parts.q: A POS console is replaced and the entire database must be read into memory. Which mode of access should be used? Explain briefly.
parts.ms: Sequential access (1); every record is needed, so reading from the beginning in order is efficient (1)

sq.src: Textbook A1 Ch2 Chapter Exercise LQ3 (p.55)

sq.q: ABC Secondary School stores data about students, teachers and classrooms.

parts.q: Using this school as an example, describe each level of the data hierarchy from the lowest to the highest.
parts.ms:
Field: one attribute, e.g. a student's name (1)
Record: all fields of one student (1)
File/table: all student records with the same structure (1)
Database: related files e.g. STUDENT, TEACHER, CLASSROOM tables (1)

parts.q: State one advantage of using a DBMS rather than a spreadsheet for this data.
parts.ms: Organises, stores and retrieves large amounts of data efficiently / links related tables reducing redundancy (1)

sq.q: An online form for a volunteer activity has fields: Student ID, Name, Sex, Age, Phone number, Email, Start date, End date.

parts.q: For each of Sex, Age and Phone number, name one suitable validation check and give the rule.
parts.ms:
Sex: fixed value check, M or F (1)
Age: range check, e.g. greater than 12 (or type check: number) (1)
Phone: length check, 8 digits (1)

parts.q: Name the check that compares Start date and End date and state the rule.
parts.ms: Consistency check (1); end date must come after the start date (1)

parts.q: Suggest how the interface could be changed to reduce errors in the Sex and Start date fields.
parts.ms: Use a drop-down list/radio buttons for Sex (1); a date picker for Start date (1)

parts.q: Explain why data that passes all validation checks may still be incorrect.
parts.ms: Validation only checks data is reasonable, e.g. age 15 typed as 16 still passes (1)

sq.q: A Hong Kong identity card number consists of one or two letters, six digits and a check digit.

parts.q: Describe the steps to check whether an HKID number is valid.
parts.ms:
Add a space in front if only one letter; convert letters A=10…Z=35, space=36 (1)
Multiply characters by weights 9 to 1 and sum (1)
Valid if weighted sum divisible by 11 (1)

parts.q: Find the check digit for Y147036. Show your working.
State one type of error a check digit can detect.
parts.ms: Transcription error / transposition error when entering the number (1)

sq.q: Data is sent between two computers as 7-bit binary codes plus one parity bit.

parts.q: Explain how an even parity check works.
parts.ms: A parity bit is appended so that the total number of 1s is even (1); the receiver counts the 1s and an odd count shows an error (1)

parts.q: Give the 8-bit code for 1010101 using odd parity.
Explain why a code that passes the parity check may still contain errors.
parts.ms: If two (an even number of) bits are changed (1), the number of 1s stays even/odd, so the error is not detected (1)

sq.q: A library database table BOOK stores 50 000 records. Staff often search by TITLE.

parts.q: Explain how indexing the TITLE field speeds up searching.
parts.ms: An index table stores TITLE and a pointer to each record (1); it is sorted (1); each comparison eliminates about half the entries, so far fewer records are checked than a row-by-row search (1)

parts.q: Give two disadvantages of indexing.
parts.ms: Index must be updated when records are added or titles change, taking time (1); extra storage space (1)

parts.q: Should every field be indexed? Explain.
parts.ms: No, only frequently searched fields, because each index costs update time and space (1)

sq.q: A company compares magnetic tape and hard disk for its storage.

parts.q: State the file access method used by each.
parts.ms: Magnetic tape: sequential access (1); hard disk: direct access (1)

parts.q: Give two reasons why magnetic tape is used for backups.
parts.ms: Lower unit price per capacity (1); longer lifespan / higher portability (1)

parts.q: Why is a hard disk better for frequently used data?
parts.ms: Direct access gives a stable and generally higher access speed (1)

sq.q: Two errors were found in data entered into a school system: (i) '$15' was stored as '$51'; (ii) a parent gave a non-existent email address.

parts.q: Name each type of error.
parts.ms: (i) transposition error (1); (ii) data source error (1)

parts.q: Suggest one method to reduce each error.
parts.ms: (i) proofreading / double data entry (1); (ii) send an activation code to the email to be entered (1)

parts.q: Explain the meaning of 'garbage in, garbage out'.
parts.ms: If unreliable or incorrect data is input (1), the output information is useless (1)
